titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 7/2010 (ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ އިދާރީ ދާއިރާތައް ލާމަރުކަޒީ އުޞޫލުން ހިންގުމުގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް 19 ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This amends the Decentralization Act so the Cabinet can take land or property away from an island or city council for government development projects, whatever other laws say. Once the ministry notifies the council, the land becomes state property. Before that, the ministry must publish project details, consult the council, and give the council and the public at least 14 days to comment. Councils must cooperate with these projects, may not block them without good reason, and must hand over land even before a land use plan is approved.
whyItMatters: Island and city councils lose some control over land in their area when the government wants it for projects. Residents get a 14-day window to object, and lawful investors on the land get compensation.
keyProvisions: Section 56-2(b): the Cabinet may decide to remove land or places from a council's jurisdiction for government development projects; after the ministry notifies the council, the land passes from the council's ownership to full state control.

Section 56-2(d): before removal, the ministry must publish details of the land and the project, share them with the council, and give the council and any other person at least 14 days to send views or complaints, then make any changes needed.
Reasonable compensation, set by the Finance Ministry, must be paid for any lawful investment the council or a third party has made on the land.
Section 107-2: even before an island or city land use plan is approved, the council must hand over land the government needs for a development project.
Sections 131-1 and 131-2: councils must fully cooperate with government projects for the public benefit, and must not obstruct them without reasonable cause or make decisions that stop them.
All property of former atoll councils that moved to the Local Government Authority under Law 22/2025 transfers to the Ministry of Finance.
whoIsAffected: Island and city councils, residents of islands where government projects are planned, and investors using council land.
